newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss banks turn up only $3.4 mln in Mobutu assets.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks turn up only $3.4 mln in Mobutu assets.

text.p: Swiss banks have found only $3.4 million in assets of toppled Zairean ruler Mobutu Sese Seko including foreign shares, bonds, securities and a safe deposit box yet to be opened, banking watchdogs said on Tuesday.

The sums banks reported after a search ordered by Berne for the frozen assets were just a fraction of the billions Kinshasa's new rulers say Mobutu has stashed away with Swiss banks, among the world's most secretive.

The Federal Banking Commission, Switzerland's banking supervisor, said in a statement that six banks reported assets worth 4.8 million Swiss francs held by Mobutu, his family or people and companies associated with them.

FBC deputy director Daniel Zuberbuehler said the commission considered the matter closed, although he acknowledged that returning the funds to Kinshasa's new government could take years under Swiss legal procedures.
"As the banking supervisor, basically we are satisfied. I don't think we can order any other search. I think we have done more than anyone else in the world," Zuberbuehler told Reuters.
Asked how long it may take to return the money, he said: "It could take years."

Switzerland froze Mobutu's assets, including a sprawling luxury 30-room mansion in Lausanne with a market value of more than $5.5 milion, last month hours after the veteran strongman fled his capital Kinshasa.
The rebels who swept to power in the vast central African country have also called on the United States, France, Belgium, Austria, Liechtenstein and Portugal to follow suit.
When Mobutu was toppled, Berne ordered all Swiss banks to report whether they or their foreign subsidiaries were holding wealth for Mobutu, his family or their associates.

"All 406 banks answered on time. Six banks have reported such assets worth a total amount of 4,786,570.00 Swiss francs. These assets have been frozen on the basis of the Federal Council's decree of May 17, 1997," the banking watchdog said.
The new government in Kinshasa has sought legal assistance from Berne in tracking down reports that Mobutu stashed billions of dollars of looted national wealth abroad.
In a newspaper interview last week, new Justice Minister Celestin Lwangi alleged Mobutu had 11 billion Swiss francs here.
But Zuberbuehler dismissed "these wild stories".
"There are no billions. Of course they can say anything but these would be dreams. It would be nice if Mobutu had billions here, but he probably has spent the money."
The Federal Banking Commission declined to name the banks holding Mobutu's funds.
But Zuberbuehler said the bulk of the money, more than four million Swiss francs, was at one bank in two "fat accounts".
"This bank will receive a letter from the banking commission and it will have to explain itself. It will have to explain how its internal guidelines were implemented," he said.
The rest of the assets were in small accounts at banks where the management was not aware of their existence. One was dormant and had seen no movement for more than 20 years.

In a rare glimpse of the secretive Swiss bank vaults, Zuberbuehler said a safe deposit box was also mentioned by one of the banks, but added: "You wouldn't have big amounts of assets in a safe deposit box."

Jean Ziegler, a Socialist member of parliament and a fierce critic of the government and banks in the simmering crisis over allegations that Swiss banks hoarded the assets of Jews murdered by Hitler, accused the bankers of lying over Mobutu's wealth.
"This is grotesque," he told Reuters. "Swiss banks lied once again to defend their client Mobutu. It's catastrophic they haven't learnt anything from the crisis over Holocaust funds."
"All indications lead us to believe that Mobutu has at least $4 billion in Switzerland. This is a financial empire and it is here in Switzerland."
--- Reuters Geneva Newsroom 41-22-733 38 31
